{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6kCbYi4uA7WxZsETJY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0195HEVhatfNs8z7RqoBw4Ja","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-005/2026-07-24T151328Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why production hits `mainnet.base.org` and how to settle it\n\n## The exact chain\n\n**1. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at build time, not read at runtime.**\nNext.js does not read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in the browser. During\n`next build`, webpack **statically string-replaces** every\n`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reference with the literal value present in the\nbuild environment's shell at that moment, then bakes it into the JS bundle.\nThere is no server-side `process.env` lookup afterward — especially not for a\nstatic export on generic hosting, where no Node process runs at all. The value\nis frozen into the shipped `.js` chunks.\n\n**2. Dev vs. prod diverge because the value comes from *the build host's* env.**\n- Dev machines: the developer has `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in their local\n  `.env.local` / shell, so `yarn start` (or `next dev`) inlines the paid URL.\n  Everything routes through the paid RPC → no 429s.\n- Production: the CI/build step that produced the static bundle **did not have\n  `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` set**. So the compiler inlined it as `undefined`.\n  The `.env.local` on the deploy host is irrelevant — it's never consulted by a\n  static export. The paid URL simply never entered the bundle.\n\n**3. Undefined override collapses `rpcOverrides`.**\n```ts\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL }\n// becomes, in the prod bundle:\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: undefined }\n```\n\n**4. The transport falls back to the chain's default public RPC.**\nIn `wagmiConfig.tsx`'s `client({ chain })`, the override is read as\n`rpcOverrideUrl = scaffoldConfig.rpcOverrides?.[chain.id]`. It's `undefined`, so\nthe `if (rpcOverrideUrl)` branch is skipped and `rpcFallbacks` stays/ends up as\na bare `[http()]` (or public-first). **`http()` called with no URL uses\n`chain.rpcUrls.default.http[0]`**, which for Base is exactly\n`https://mainnet.base.org`. Every production request pours onto the public\nendpoint → 429s.\n\n## The one operational check that settles whether the fix is real\n\n**Grep the deployed production bundle (or watch the prod DevTools Network tab)\nfor the RPC hostname — do not trust source, `.env`, or a redeploy.**\n\nBecause the URL is inlined, the truth is in the shipped artifact:\n\n```bash\n# against the built/deployed static assets:\ngrep -r \"your-paid-rpc-host\" .next/  # or curl the live .js chunks\ngrep -r \"mainnet.base.org\" .next/\n```\n\nIf the paid host appears as a string literal → the env var was present **at\nbuild time** and the fix is real. If you still see `mainnet.base.org` /\n`undefined` → the rebuild didn't have the var. This distinguishes the only two\nfailure modes that a config diff can't: (a) redeploying the *same* bundle\nwithout rebuilding, and (b) rebuilding in a CI environment that still lacks the\nvar. Equivalently: load production, open the Network tab, and confirm the\nJSON-RPC POSTs go to the paid host, not `mainnet.base.org`.\n\n## The second, transport-level trap in `wagmiConfig.tsx`\n\nEven once the env var is fixed and the override is present, the transport is:\n\n```ts\nrpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];   // note the bare http()\nreturn createClient({ chain, transport: fallback(rpcFallbacks) });\n```\n\nThe bare **`http()` (= public `mainnet.base.org`) is permanently kept in the\n`fallback()` chain** as the second transport. viem's `fallback` transport\n**fails over to the next transport on any error from the primary — including a\n429**. So under load, when the paid RPC rate-limits or times out, requests\nsilently roll onto the public endpoint anyway (and with `rank` enabled, viem\nalso periodically probes the ranked transports, touching the public RPC even\nwhen it isn't primary). The public RPC is never actually removed from rotation;\nfixing the env var only changes *which* transport is tried first.\n\n**Related consequence (same root):** Scaffold-ETH always appends `mainnet`\n(chain id 1) to `enabledChains` for ENS / ETH-price resolution, but\n`rpcOverrides` only keys `base.id`. During\n`next build`, webpack **statically string-replaces** every\n`process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reference with the literal value present in the\nbuild environment's shell at that moment, then bakes it into the JS bundle.\nThere is no server-side `process.env` lookup afterward — especially not for a\nstatic export on generic hosting, where no Node process runs at all. The value\nis frozen into the shipped `.js` chunks.\n\n**2. Dev vs. prod diverge because the value comes from *the build host's* env.**\n- Dev machines: the developer has `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` in their local\n  `.env.local` / shell, so `yarn start` (or `next dev`) inlines the paid URL.\n  Everything routes through the paid RPC → no 429s.\n- Production: the CI/build step that produced the static bundle **did not have\n  `NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL` set**. So the compiler inlined it as `undefined`.\n  The `.env.local` on the deploy host is irrelevant — it's never consulted by a\n  static export. The paid URL simply never entered the bundle.\n\n**3. Undefined override collapses `rpcOverrides`.**\n```ts\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RPC_URL }\n// becomes, in the prod bundle:\nrpcOverrides: { [chains.base.id]: undefined }\n```\n\n**4. The transport falls back to the chain's default public RPC.**\nIn `wagmiConfig.tsx`'s `client({ chain })`, the override is read as\n`rpcOverrideUrl = scaffoldConfig.rpcOverrides?.[chain.id]`. It's `undefined`, so\nthe `if (rpcOverrideUrl)` branch is skipped and `rpcFallbacks` stays/ends up as\na bare `[http()]` (or public-first). **`http()` called with no URL uses\n`chain.rpcUrls.default.http[0]`**, which for Base is exactly\n`https://mainnet.base.org`. Every production request pours onto the public\nendpoint → 429s.\n\n## The one operational check that settles whether the fix is real\n\n**Grep the deployed production bundle (or watch the prod DevTools Network tab)\nfor the RPC hostname — do not trust source, `.env`, or a redeploy.**\n\nBecause the URL is inlined, the truth is in the shipped artifact:\n\n```bash\n# against the built/deployed static assets:\ngrep -r \"your-paid-rpc-host\" .next/  # or curl the live .js chunks\ngrep -r \"mainnet.base.org\" .next/\n```\n\nIf the paid host appears as a string literal → the env var was present **at\nbuild time** and the fix is real. If you still see `mainnet.base.org` /\n`undefined` → the rebuild didn't have the var. This distinguishes the only two\nfailure modes that a config diff can't: (a) redeploying the *same* bundle\nwithout rebuilding, and (b) rebuilding in a CI environment that still lacks the\nvar. Equivalently: load production, open the Network tab, and confirm the\nJSON-RPC POSTs go to the paid host, not `mainnet.base.org`.\n\n## The second, transport-level trap in `wagmiConfig.tsx`\n\nEven once the env var is fixed and the override is present, the transport is:\n\n```ts\nrpcFallbacks = [http(rpcOverrideUrl), http()];   // note the bare http()\nreturn createClient({ chain, transport: fallback(rpcFallbacks) });\n```\n\nThe bare **`http()` (= public `mainnet.base.org`) is permanently kept in the\n`fallback()` chain** as the second transport. viem's `fallback` transport\n**fails over to the next transport on any error from the primary — including a\n429**. So under load, when the paid RPC rate-limits or times out, requests\nsilently roll onto the public endpoint anyway (and with `rank` enabled, viem\nalso periodically probes the ranked transports, touching the public RPC even\nwhen it isn't primary). The public RPC is never actually removed from rotation;\nfixing the env var only changes *which* transport is tried first.\n\n**Related consequence (same root):** Scaffold-ETH always appends `mainnet`\n(chain id 1) to `enabledChains` for ENS / ETH-price resolution, but\n`rpcOverrides` only keys `base.id`. So all mainnet requests hit `http()` with no\noverride — Ethereum's default public RPC — regardless of the Base fix. If you\nwant zero public-RPC traffic, add an override for **every** enabled chain and\ndrop/replace the bare `http()` failover.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
